assessment.nobel_worthiness: Gut-derived GLP-1 physiology defined glucose-dependent insulin secretion and led to incretin drugs that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity treatment. The discovery is clear, original, and has had very large, field-changing clinical and physiological impact.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 biology and secretion), Drucker (GLP-1 actions, GLP-2, DPP-4 biology) and Mojsov (identification of the biologically active GLP-1 form) form a plausible three-person set; Knudsen's drug-development role and the contributions of others such as Habener are real competing claims, so the set is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, extensive human outcome data and widespread clinical use make recognition timely and the interpretation stable.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit between basic discoverers and the pharmaceutical development (Knudsen) is contested and only three can be named.
Priority for the active GLP-1 peptide sequence is disputed in the literature; I have not independently verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered chimeric antigen receptor T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and created a new therapeutic modality, with strong conceptual and clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early CAR design with costimulation (CD28) and June the clinical translation with 4-1BB CAR-T in leukemia; Rosenberg's adoptive cell therapy work is foundational but distinct, so a two-person set seems cleaner.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and over a decade of follow-up support maturity, though long-term safety, solid-tumour limits and competing contributions (Eshhar, Kuwana, Gross) leave some questions.
uncertainties: Earlier CAR concept work by Eshhar and others may compete for credit; not in the credited list.
Whether a prize would cover cell therapy broadly or the CAR specifically is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Channelrhodopsin-based optogenetics enabled causal, millisecond-scale control of defined cell types and has become a foundational experimental tool across neuroscience and physiology, with growing therapeutic use (vision restoration).
assessment.attribution: The discovery of the channelrhodopsin light-gated channel (Bamberg, Nagel, Hegemann) is the most clearly decisive step; Boyden, Deisseroth and Miesenböck were decisive in neuronal implementation and demonstration, so a laureate set excluding them would be contentious.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and deeply embedded in research for 15-plus years; clinical translation is early but the tool impact is established.
uncertainties: Tension between molecular discoverers and neuronal-application pioneers; at most three of six credited names can be recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The cGAS-STING pathway revealed how cytosolic DNA is sensed to trigger innate immunity, interferon responses and inflammation, with implications for infection, autoimmunity, cancer and ageing. The mechanistic clarity is high.
assessment.attribution: Chen identified cGAS and cGAMP as the second messenger; Barber identified STING; these are the two decisive steps. Others (e.g., Ishikawa, and earlier work from other groups, cyclic dinucleotide biology) have lesser or different claims.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed mechanistically, though therapeutic payoff (STING agonists/inhibitors) is not yet realized, which may argue for waiting.
uncertainties: Clinical translation has been disappointing so far.
Credit of related discoveries (cyclic dinucleotide signalling, Vance and others) is not covered by the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic from the ER to the nucleus, with broad relevance to proteostasis, secretory-cell physiology and disease. It is a clean, original, conceptually important discovery.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the central figures (Ire1/Hac1 splicing, Hac1/XBP1 and ATF6 pathways); Walter's group also elucidated Ire1 and later ISR work. A two-person prize is coherent, with Ron/Harding as possible alternative claimants not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is thoroughly confirmed over decades; disease relevance is broad but therapeutic validation is still emerging.
uncertainties: Direct clinical impact is modest compared with other candidates.
Relationship to the integrated stress response and PERK work may complicate boundaries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR as the central regulator of cell growth and nutrient sensing is a major conceptual advance with consequences for metabolism, cancer, ageing and immunology. The originality of the yeast TOR discovery is clear.
assessment.attribution: Hall's discovery of TOR in yeast is the core; Sabatini's mTOR identification and nutrient-sensing mechanisms are important extensions, while Schreiber's rapamycin chemical biology and Heitman/Hall's early work are competing claims.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed; clinical use of rapalogs exists, though many promised applications remain partial.
uncertainties: Credit split between Hall, Sabatini, Schreiber and others (Brown, Sabers, Heitman) is unresolved; Sabatini's ongoing controversies are not evaluated here.
Whether the recognition should centre on the discovery or on rapamycin pharmacology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: HPV virus-like particle vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical and other cancers; a landmark of preventive medicine with real population-level effects on disease incidence.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the L1 VLP platform; Frazer's contributions (with Zhou) to VLP production and the vaccine are decisive; Zhou's early death and Zur Hausen's earlier prize on HPV-cancer link shape the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Population-level reductions in CIN and cervical cancer are now documented, so evidence is mature; however the 2008 prize partly recognised the HPV link.
uncertainties: Overlap in priority with Jian Zhou (deceased) and Frazer's role relative to the VLP developers.
Overlap with 2008 prize may reduce novelty in the committee's view.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Organoids derived from adult Lgr5 stem cells created long-lived, genetically stable human epithelial culture systems with broad use in disease modelling, drug screening and personalised medicine.
assessment.attribution: Clevers led the Lgr5 stem-cell and organoid work with Sato as first author of the foundational intestinal organoid paper; a two-person set is coherent, though broader organoid pioneers (Sasai, Lancaster) have separate claims.
assessment.maturity: Rapid adoption but clinical impact is still emerging, so recognition may be somewhat early; core method is widely replicated.
uncertainties: Relation to pluripotent-stem-cell organoids and other organoid lineages is unresolved.
